aspects.says: BCD can't carry letters: a letter in a BCD field silently becomes another digit, so track 2 is normalised to = before it is set.
basis: section:13.4 An Odd Number of BCD Digits Needs a Filler, on the Same Side at Both Ends
aspects.reason: the page shows the effect; a practice would only replace one character before a set

aspects.says: Variable-length binary field packagers don't check their maximum, and a BCD prefix too short for the length is written wrong without an error.
basis: section:13.3 A Length Prefix Counts Digits or Bytes, and Only the Specification Says Which

aspects.says: An unpack error names a field after the wrong one, and an unpack can succeed with shifted values; the first field whose value is wrong is the row to fix.
basis: section:13.7 An Unpack Error Points Past the Field That Is Wrong

aspects.says: An odd number of BCD digits carries a filler nibble whose side is the pad setting, and both ends must agree; only odd-length values are affected.
basis: section:13.4 An Odd Number of BCD Digits Needs a Filler, on the Same Side at Both Ends

aspects.says: A packager name with jar: is read from the classpath; a plain name is a file path relative to the directory the JVM started in.
basis: section:13.6.1 Where the File Comes From

aspects.says: A field packager's class name gives the encoding, the length rule and the type of a specification row; B means BCD, and IFA_BINARY sends bytes as hex text.
basis: section:13.2 A Field Packager's Name Spells Out the Specification's Row

aspects.says: The bytes carry no field boundaries, so a receiver whose layout differs in one field reads every later field from the wrong place.
basis: section:13.1 The Bytes Carry No Field Boundaries, Only the Packager Knows Them

aspects.says: Field packagers are a padder, an interpreter and a prefixer, and a combination no stock class offers can be built from them.
basis: section:13.2.1 Classes Are Combinations, and You Can Make Your Own
aspects.reason: a custom combination is needed only for an unusual specification; the stock classes cover the practice's rows, and the page shows the pattern

aspects.says: A BCD length prefix counts digits for numeric fields and bytes for text and binary fields, and the wrong choice can misread a message without an error.
basis: section:13.3 A Length Prefix Counts Digits or Bytes, and Only the Specification Says Which

aspects.says: A round trip can't find a wrong layout because the packager reads back what it wrote; a test from the specification's sample bytes, checking values, bytes used and bytes repacked, can.
basis: section:13.5 A Round Trip Can't Check the Layout; the Specification's Sample Can

aspects.says: GenericPackager XML names the same field packager classes and packs the same bytes; a sub-field layout can carry a bitmap of its own.
basis: section:13.6 The XML Names the Same Classes, and Is Read From the Classpath
aspects.reason: writing sub-field XML is practised in unit c6, and the XML rows are the same choices the regional-packager practice grades in Java
